newsitem.title: TURKEY: Sabanci group to sell 8.5 mln T of cement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sabanci group to sell 8.5 mln T of cement in 1997.

text.p: The cement division of Turkish Sabanci Holding which includes Akcansa, the country's biggest cement firm, plans to sell 8.534 million tonnes of cement in 1997, a senior company official said.
"We will use more than 80 percent of the group's total 10.82-million-tonne cement capacity and sell all of the output," Ayduk Celenk, the president of Sabanci group's cement division, told Reuters.
Akcansa has a six-million-tonne annual production capacity and targets 5.2 million tonnes of sales.

The company, a joint venture by Sabanci Holding and Belgian Cimenteries CBR SA, operates two plants in western Turkey. CBR's Canakkale Cimento and Sabanci's Akcimento had merged last September to form Akcansa.

Another Sabanci subsidiary Cimsa, plans to sell 2.424 million tonnes of cement in 1997 from its two plants in central Kayseri town and the southern port town of Mersin. The company has a total output capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.
Two other smaller cement makers in the group -- Oysa-Nigde Cimento and Oysa-Iskenderun Cimento target a total 910,000 tonnes of sales this year, against a total annual capacity of 1.1 million tonnes.
Sabanci and Turkish armed forces pension fund OYAK are partners in Oysa-Nigde and Oysa-Iskenderun.

The four cement companies, including Oyak and CBR ventures, have a total 10.82 million tonnes of output capacity which is approximately 25 percent of Turkey's overall cement production capacity of 42 million tonnes.
The Sabanci cement division operates six plants in total Turkey's Marmara, Mediterranean, central regions.
"We are considering setting up new plants or making acquisitions to expand our activities wherever necessary in new regions (the Aegean and southeast)," Celenk said.
He said the Sabanci group estimated an eight percent or two-million-tonne growth in Turkey's cement output in 1997, over last year's 35.23 million tonnes which was up 6.3 percent from 1995.
"Turkey is a good market for cement and this attracts foreign investments in this sector. It will continue to be a good cement consumer until the year 2020," Celenk said.
He added that major infrastructure investments would have to be undertaken even if the annual population growth rate was reduced to one percent by 2010 from more than two at present.

"Annual cement consumption per capita is 450 kg in developed countries, so Turkey's yearly consumption will be 40 million tonnes in 2010 when the population reaches 80 million. Before that, demand per capita will peak at 800 kg," Celenk said.
He added that Turkey should turn to imports to meet excess demand until 2020 instead of raising the current output capacity via new investments to avoid facing idle capacity after 2020.
